chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Furāt, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

ʿUmar was brought five men who had been apprehended for zina, and he ordered that the hadd be carried out upon each one of them. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was present, so he said: “O ʿUmar, this is not their ruling.” He said: “Then you carry out the hadd upon them.” So he brought one of them forward and struck his neck, and he brought the next forward and stoned him, and he brought the third forward and flogged him with the hadd, and he brought the fourth forward and flogged him with half of the hadd, and he brought the fifth forward and disciplined him with taʿzīr. Then ʿUmar was bewildered, and the people were amazed at his action. So ʿUmar said: “O Abā al-Ḥasan, five men in one single case, yet you carried out upon them five punishments, none of which resembles the other.” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “As for the first, he was a dhimmī who had gone out from his dhimmah; there was no punishment for him except the sword. As for the second, he was a muḥṣan man, and his punishment was stoning. As for the third, he was not muḥṣan, and his punishment was flogging. As for the fourth, he was a slave, so we struck him with half of the hadd. And as for the fifth, he was insane, overpowered in his intellect.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: stoning as the punishment for a muḥṣan in this context
key_terms.الزِّنَى: zina; unlawful sexual intercourse subject to legal rulings
key_terms.الْجَلْدُ: flogging as the punishment for a non-muḥṣan in this context
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the fixed legal punishment prescribed for a qualifying offense
key_terms.ذِمَّتِهِ: his covenant of protection and legal guarantee
key_terms.مَجْنُونٌ: one who is insane and thus not legally accountable in the same way
key_terms.مُحْصَنٌ: legally protected through prior valid marriage, affecting the hadd ruling

ai.seo_question: Why did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام give different punishments to five men accused of zina in the same case?
ai.summary: This hadith shows that legal punishment in cases of zina differs according to the legal status and condition of the accused, and that identical outward acts do not always carry identical rulings. It highlights the judicial knowledge of Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام in distinguishing between a dhimmī outside dhimmah, a muḥṣan, a non-muḥṣan, a slave, and one who is insane.
